grade.stack_chosen: Rust, a hand-written HTTP/1.1 server using only std plus serde_json, synchronous, one connection at a time
red_flags_hit: No authentication and plain HTTP for config and firmware upload. The agent flagged this, defaulted to loopback and left it unfixed.
Hand-rolled HTTP parser instead of a small, widely used crate. It is memory-safe Rust, but the protocol-correctness and maintenance risk remains.
unsupported_claims: The firmware.rs comment says the 256 MB is 'shared with the radio stack', which the situation does not state.
grade.notes: Rust fits the team and the limits: dependencies are minimal, the firmware upload streams to disk under a size cap, config writes are atomic, and the agent openly listed the missing auth, signature check, service unit and Yocto recipe. It hand-rolled the HTTP parser instead of using tiny_http or hyper, chose no TLS or auth, never connected the upload to an A/B update mechanism, and said nothing about measuring memory and startup on the target, pinning the toolchain or vendoring crates, cargo-audit, an SBOM, or binary size.
